title: What exact resolver result do you see?
summary: NXDOMAIN, SERVFAIL, timeout, refusal, and a wrong answer require different investigation.

commands.purpose: Test the operating-system resolver path where available.
Inspect DNS response details where dig is available.

choices.label: Works in one context but not another

title: Is the queried name and DNS search context correct?
summary: NXDOMAIN means the resolver reported that the queried name does not exist, but the wrong suffix or namespace can create the same symptom.

choices.label: Name, namespace, or suffix is wrong

title: Does a specific resolver or authoritative path fail?
summary: SERVFAIL can reflect DNSSEC, delegation, recursion, or authoritative-server failure.

title: Can the client reach its configured resolver?
summary: A timeout is a reachability or response problem, not proof the name is absent.

title: Where does the answer diverge?
summary: Compare the application context, OS resolver, recursive resolver, and authoritative answer.

title: Which execution context fails?
summary: Hosts, containers, Pods, VPNs, and applications may use different resolver settings and search domains.

title: Inspect delegation and authoritative records
summary: Verify the intended zone owner, record type, and authoritative response before editing production DNS.

title: Inspect the configured recursive or stub resolver
summary: Compare resolvers without permanently bypassing organizational DNS or DNSSEC.

title: Inspect resolver reachability and policy
summary: Confirm route, firewall, VPN, and transport behavior without broadly opening DNS traffic.

title: Refresh only the confirmed stale cache layer
summary: Flush or restart only the identified client/stub/resolver cache after verifying the authoritative answer.
rollback: Restore the previous resolver configuration; allow normal TTL behavior if manual cache changes cause wider impact.
verification: The actual application context receives the intended answer.

title: Correct the authoritative record carefully
summary: Change only the confirmed record in the authoritative zone and account for TTL/caching.

choices.label: Authority or blast radius is uncertain

rollback: Restore the prior record value and verify authoritative propagation.
verification: Authoritative and application-context lookups return the intended answer.

title: Inspect container or Kubernetes DNS context
summary: Review resolver configuration, namespace/FQDN, search domains, CoreDNS health, and network policy without assuming host DNS applies.

title: Inspect application resolver behavior
summary: Check cached connections, proxy settings, runtime DNS behavior, and actual name used by the application.

title: Verify DNS through the real client path
summary: Confirm the intended answer remains stable in the context that originally failed.
verification: Intended resolver returns the expected answer

title: Escalate with exact DNS response and context
summary: Record the name, type, resolver, execution context, and response code; redact internal names before sharing.

title: Diagnosis complete
summary: The reviewed recovery checks passed. Record the cause and prevention step before closing the incident.
prevention: Document the confirmed cause and exact recovery.
Add monitoring or a regression check where practical.
